free_tier.stated: The deepest H100 discount found anywhere in this class, read live and anonymously. NVIDIA H100 NVLink in eu-north1 at USD 0.79 per GPU-hour against USD 4.50 on-demand, which is 17.6 per cent of on-demand, a 5.70 times reduction. The same page at the same moment shows H200 at USD 0.89 in us-central1 against USD 5.40 on-demand (16.5 per cent, 6.07 times), B200 at USD 3.60 in us-central1, and B300 at USD 5.89 in eu-west2 and us-north1. The H100 price had been effective since 9 October 2026 17:01, so it was stable for 13 days at the time of reading.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: USD 0.79 an H100-hour means USD 300 of credit buys 380 H100-hours, which is the largest measured H100 budget in the corpus at any identity cost.
limits_note: The price is the floor of a dynamic range that can rise to one cent below on-demand every 15 minutes, and the deep rates are single-region, so the failure mode is the rate moving rather than the capacity being unreachable.

notes: This number is better than every third-party H100 spot rate found and it is measurable with no account, which makes it the reference point the rest of the class should be judged against. It is also 2.8 times cheaper than Verda's flat 50 per cent H100 spot at USD 2.235. The risk is entirely in the dynamic clause: the range ceiling is one cent under USD 4.50, so a run without a pricing policy has unbounded cost, and a pricing policy that caps it converts the price risk into a stop. H100 is single-region (eu-north1), so there is no region to move to when the price rises. qualifies-with-caveat via a05-spot. The one recorded is the better-evidenced.
